market_context: United States; opened cheese in a home refrigerator
title: How to store cheese after opening

seo.title: How to store cheese after opening
seo.meta_description: Hard cheese needs cold storage and wrapping that limits drying without trapping too much moisture. Soft and fresh cheese should be tightly covered and used sooner; the type of cheese determines the timeline.
seo.search_intent: Explain how to wrap, refrigerate and store different cheeses after opening.

excerpt: Opened cheese should go back into the refrigerator protected from drying and contamination. Hard cheese keeps best when wrapped without trapping heavy condensation; soft and fresh cheese should stay covered and be used sooner. The cheese type matters as much as the date you opened it.
content_html:
The worst place for opened cheese is usually one of two extremes: fully exposed to refrigerator air, where it dries out and absorbs odors, or sealed with excess trapped moisture, where the surface can become wet and deteriorate faster. Good storage balances the two.

Start with steady refrigeration

Once opened, return cheese to the refrigerator. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or below. High-moisture fresh and soft cheeses need more careful handling and generally have shorter storage windows than hard cheeses.

How to wrap hard and semi-hard cheese

For a block of cheddar, Gouda, Swiss or Parmesan, protect the cut surface without trapping lots of condensation. Cheese paper or waxed paper works well; the wrapped piece can then go into a loose container or bag to slow further drying.

If plastic wrap is all you have, fit it closely and replace it if moisture builds up. It is still much better than leaving the cheese uncovered.

Soft cheese needs a different approach

Brie, ricotta, cottage cheese and other high-moisture cheeses should stay in their original resealable package or a clean covered container. Do not leave cut or spooned surfaces exposed.

USDA guidance gives about 1 week in the refrigerator for many soft cheeses and about 3 to 4 weeks after opening for hard cheeses such as cheddar, Swiss and Parmesan. Manufacturer instructions can be shorter and should take priority.

Where in the refrigerator?

A stable interior shelf or produce drawer is usually better than the door, where temperature rises and falls every time the refrigerator opens. A slightly more humid zone can also reduce drying in hard cheese.

Keep odors and contamination separate

Cheese readily picks up strong aromas. Keep it away from cut onions, fish and other pungent foods, and use clean knives. Avoid cutting cheese with a utensil that has just touched another food and then returning it to the block.

What about unexpected mold?

Hard cheeses can sometimes be salvaged by cutting well around a small spot of unwanted mold, while soft and fresh cheeses are much more likely to require discarding because contamination can extend below the surface. That is different from the intentional molds on Brie or blue cheese.

The storage rule

Hard cheese: cold, wrapped and protected from drying. Soft or fresh cheese: cold, covered and used sooner. Always follow a shorter use-after-opening instruction when the package provides one.

faq.question: How long does opened hard cheese last?
faq.answer: USDA guidance gives about 3 to 4 weeks after opening for hard cheeses such as cheddar, Swiss and Parmesan when refrigerated.

faq.question: How long does opened soft cheese last?
faq.answer: Many soft cheeses have a general refrigerator window of about one week, though high-moisture fresh cheeses may have shorter manufacturer instructions.

faq.question: Should cheese be wrapped in paper or plastic?
faq.answer: Hard cheese often does well in cheese or waxed paper that limits drying without trapping too much condensation. Plastic wrap is acceptable when fitted closely and changed if it becomes wet.
